GOAL (design review Step 5, unresolved-cue escalation): today a scene's authored cue (FactDelivery.cue_text) is shown once, then the fact id goes into RuntimeState.delivered_cue_ids and is never shown again. ScenePacing.nudge_after_turns is validated in models.py but unused by the engine. Implement ONE stronger pointer per eligible unresolved reveal per scene visit, scheduled at nudge_after_turns.

READ FIRST: storygame/runtime/engine.py (_activate_pacing ~600-660 where the cue is staged, turn() ~200-290 where the staged cue is marked delivered, _cue_reveal_available, _ranked_cue_fact_ids, _record_attempt), storygame/runtime/state.py (RuntimeState, RuntimeSnapshot, snapshot/restore), storygame/runtime/cloudflare.py _compose_staged_cue (~1150), storygame/story_package/models.py FactDelivery and ScenePacing, tests/test_staged_cues.py, tests/test_cue_text_safety.py, tests/test_pacing_handoff.py, tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py, tests/test_attempt_bundle.py.

BUILD:
1. models.py: FactDelivery gets optional `escalation_text: str | None = None` (non-empty if set, same validator style as cue_text). The loader must apply to escalation_text the same player-safety checks it applies to cue_text today (find where cue_text is checked, e.g. tests/test_cue_text_safety.py shows the rule: a cue must not name an unrevealed secret). Do not edit the story data; no shipped delivery sets it yet.
2. state.py: add a small frozen model (e.g. CueStage: fact_id, stage int, last_turn int, visit_entered_at int) and a tuple `cue_stages` on RuntimeState and RuntimeSnapshot, defaulting to empty so old saves/snapshots load unchanged. Keep delivered_cue_ids exactly as is (it is the stage-one history; an old save with a delivered cue and no cue_stages must behave as stage one delivered, visit unknown = treat the current visit as the delivering visit). Include cue_stages in snapshot creation and restore (rejected turns restore the pre-turn snapshot, so a rejected attempt can never consume or advance a stage), and in RuntimeState reset/new-game paths.
3. engine.py scheduling (in the same place the cue is staged, no new mutable flags outside state): a delivered cue fact becomes eligible for escalation when ALL hold: it is in delivered_cue_ids; no escalation (stage 2) has been recorded for it in this scene visit (visit = scene_entered_at_turn); turns_since_entry >= window.nudge_after_turns for the current scene; the fact is not yet asserted; the reveal is still earnable per _cue_reveal_available (this is how 'stops when earned or source spent' works: a spent alternative or an already-earned reveal makes it ineligible); the scene has not changed since the cue; and no other cue is currently staged. When eligible, stage it (staged_cue_fact_id plus an explicit stage marker stored in state, snapshot-safe). Scene re-entry is a new visit: the cue fact may show its stage-one cue again only if today's logic already allows that, and escalation counts per visit.
4. Delivery: on a committed, non-handoff turn that stays in the scene, the existing append path delivers the pointer text and records CueStage(stage=2, last_turn=turn_index, visit). Text used = delivery.escalation_text if set, else delivery.cue_text (the plan's fallback is the existing cue). It is appended through the same authored path as the cue (_compose_staged_cue), never generated by the narrator, and never put into the narrator prompt. Forced handoff delivery stays exactly as is and is recorded as assisted progress: when a handoff delivers, nothing about escalation may block or alter it. A rejected turn must not consume the staged escalation (verify via snapshot restore). If the scene changes on the delivery turn, follow the existing cue behaviour for that branch.
5. Attempt bundle (storygame/runtime/attempt_bundle.py is NOT owned, so only use its existing fields): make sure the existing cue_stage record in the bundle reflects the escalation (delivered / consumed) through the engine code that builds it in _record_attempt; if that needs a new field in attempt_bundle.py, instead describe it in notes.md and do not edit that file.
6. Tests in tests/test_cue_escalation.py, hermetic, real engine state with stubbed providers (see tests/test_design_review_fixtures.py for how to build a real 1A state), under 15 s. Use a package copy where a delivery gets escalation_text (model_copy). Timeline tests: (a) cue ignored: the escalation appears exactly once at nudge_after_turns and never again that visit, and not before; (b) reveal earned before the nudge turn: no escalation; (c) alternative spent / reveal no longer earnable: no escalation; (d) rejected attempt on the nudge turn: nothing consumed, escalation still staged and delivered on the next accepted turn; (e) snapshot/restore round trip and an old-format snapshot (no cue_stages) load; (f) scene re-entry is a new visit; (g) with escalation_text unset the existing cue text is the fallback; (h) forced handoff still delivers and is unaffected; (i) no delivered pointer text contains an unrevealed secret term for a real 1A or 2C cue (assert with the repo's existing cue-safety helper); (j) update test_missed_pointer so it now asserts the escalation instead of the defect.
7. Hard rules: no story/genre-specific branches (runtime is story-agnostic), no network, no prose-as-truth, no fact changes after rendering. Plain comments, style matching surrounding code. Narrator-facing strings: you add none.

Tests: PYTHONPATH=$PWD TMPDIR=/tmp /home/bcorfman/dev/freytag-forge/.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests/test_cue_escalation.py, then the full suite with -n auto.
